statement: Indian banks (e.g., SBI, HDFC, ICICI, PNB, Axis) and RBI never ask customers to share OTP, UPI PIN, CVV, NetBanking password, or card expiry date via SMS, email, or telephone calls.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) never opens individual bank accounts, does not hold citizen deposits, and never requests advance fees or tax payments to release lottery prizes or foreign remittances.
UPI PIN is strictly used for authorizing payments and debiting money from your bank account; entering a UPI PIN is never required to receive money, accept refunds, or collect cashbacks.

Commercial banks in India never distribute mobile banking APK files or app updates via SMS, WhatsApp, or third-party links; official apps must only be downloaded from Google Play Store or Apple App Store.
State electricity boards and Bijli Vibhag do not send disconnection threats from personal 10-digit mobile numbers demanding immediate payment via unverified phone calls or remote access apps.
The Income Tax Department issues tax refunds directly to pre-validated bank accounts and never requests debit card credentials, PINs, or banking passwords through SMS links to process refunds.
Banks never instruct customers to download remote screen-sharing tools (such as AnyDesk, TeamViewer, RustDesk, or QuickSupport) to resolve account issues or complete KYC verification.
Telecom service providers (Jio, Airtel, Vodafone Idea) do not threaten immediate SIM deactivation within 24 hours requiring customer KYC verification via personal mobile numbers.

Official bank communications regarding mandatory KYC updates never require customers to click third-party shortened URLs (such as bit.ly, tinyurl, or suspicious non-bank domains); KYC updates are performed exclusively at bank branches or via secure netbanking portals.

Law enforcement agencies, CBI, State Police, and Cyber Crime Cells never conduct 'digital arrests' via Skype or WhatsApp video calls, nor do they demand fund transfers to secret 'verification accounts'.
EPFO (Employees' Provident Fund Organisation) never asks members to share UAN credentials, Aadhaar OTP, or bank account details via SMS or phone calls for PF claim processing.
Scanning a payment QR code via PhonePe, Google Pay, Paytm, or BHIM always debits funds from the payer's account; scanning a QR code can never deposit or receive money into your account.
India Post and registered couriers do not require small re-delivery fees (e.g., Rs 10 or Rs 25) paid via external shortened SMS links containing debit card entry forms.
Credit card reward points cannot be converted into direct bank cash deposits by submitting card credentials or OTP on third-party promotional web links.
Official government welfare and loan schemes (such as PM Mudra Yojana, PM Kisan) do not demand upfront processing charges, insurance deposits, or security fees transferred via UPI.

Traffic police e-Challan payments and notifications are processed only through the official government portal (echallan.parivahan.gov.in) and never via third-party APK downloads or unverified web links.

Legitimate bank SMS alerts are sent through registered alphanumeric sender IDs (e.g., VM-SBIINB, AD-HDFCBK, AX-ICICIB) assigned by TRAI. Official bank customer dispute helplines are nationwide toll-free numbers (starting with 1800), not personal 10-digit mobile numbers.
WhatsApp or Telegram offers promising easy daily income for liking YouTube videos, rating Google Maps locations, or completing small crypto tasks are fraudulent Ponzi and task scams.
Bank accounts are never immediately blocked without prior formal statutory notices sent via official channels, and unblocking an account never requires clicking external third-party links.
UIDAI / Aadhaar demographic and document updates must be performed either at authorized Aadhaar Seva Kendras or through the official portal (myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in), never via SMS links.
